key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines weld-pool simulation and Gaussian-process surrogates to screen robotic welding conditions and control strategies for future in-space metal joining.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support welding parameter selection and adaptive control before costly flight-like testing.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates predict solver outputs.
Simulated six-axis robot adjusts power-source settings as travel speed falls near an L-seam corner.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; finite-volume re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
